answers.answer: Click is a composable Python command-line-interface toolkit for developers writing CLI applications. It offers configurable defaults, nested commands, generated help, and lazy subcommand loading.

The public click package re-exports core command/context/parameter objects, declaration decorators, types, exceptions, formatting, terminal UI, and utility functions. decorators.command constructs commands around client callbacks. parser._OptionParser handles low-level token parsing, leaving types/defaults to higher layers. testing.CliRunner supplies isolated invocation and captured results.

The library is typed Python, requires Python >=3.10, and is packaged as click (8.6.0.dev here) from src/click. pyproject.toml selects flit_core>=3.11,<4 and flit_core.buildapi. Tests use pytest; documentation uses Sphinx/MyST; tox coordinates environments. docs and tests are separate source-distribution inclusions, not separate production libraries evidenced here.
Calling a click.Command instance enters click.core.Command.__call__, which forwards to self.main. click.__init__ re-exports Command.

answers.answer: Normal path: main→make_context→parse_args→make_parser/_OptionParser.parse_args→parameter.handle_parse_result; then main→invoke→Context.invoke→callback. Dynamic boundaries include overridable methods/context_class, parameter implementations, and client callback; Group overrides dispatch. Completion/help/errors can bypass normal callback execution. This is source reasoning, not a measured runtime trace.

Parameter.add_to_parser declares the contract. Downstream breakage is speculative; exhaustive coverage is unproven.

answers.answer: Command.main accepts args, copies supplied sequences, or takes sys.argv[1:] with optional Windows expansion. _OptionParser.parse_args creates parsing state, processes options then positional arguments, and returns values, leftovers, and parameter order; '--' stops option processing. High-level parameter handling converts values and populates ctx.params. CliRunner additionally shell-splits string args before main.
